A single <a id="element&#45;restrictions&#58;syntax&#45;newlines"></a>[newline](#syntax-newlines) may be placed immediately after the <a id="element&#45;restrictions&#58;syntax&#45;start&#45;tag"></a>[start tag](#syntax-start-tag) of <a id="element&#45;restrictions&#58;the&#45;pre&#45;element"></a><code>[pre](html-language-elements-text-links--877d6146487f--8833a85fd242.md#the-pre-element)</code> and <a id="element&#45;restrictions&#58;the&#45;textarea&#45;element"></a><code>[textarea](html-language-forms-tables-templates--877d6146487f--2dfc6f632608.md#the-textarea-element)</code> elements&#46; This does not affect the processing of the element&#46; The otherwise optional <a id="element&#45;restrictions&#58;syntax&#45;newlines&#45;2"></a>[newline](#syntax-newlines) <em>must</em> be included if the element&#39;s contents themselves start with a <a id="element&#45;restrictions&#58;syntax&#45;newlines&#45;3"></a>[newline](#syntax-newlines) &#40;because otherwise the leading newline in the contents would be treated like the optional newline&#44; and ignored&#41;&#46;

<strong>Example&#58;</strong>

The following two <a id="element&#45;restrictions&#58;the&#45;pre&#45;element&#45;2"></a><code>[pre](html-language-elements-text-links--877d6146487f--8833a85fd242.md#the-pre-element)</code> blocks are equivalent&#58;

``` text
<pre>Hello</pre>
```

``` text
<pre>
Hello</pre>
```

##### <a id="cdata&#45;rcdata&#45;restrictions"></a>13&#46;1&#46;2&#46;6 Restrictions on the contents of raw text and escapable raw text elements[](#cdata-rcdata-restrictions)

The text in <a id="cdata&#45;rcdata&#45;restrictions&#58;raw&#45;text&#45;elements"></a>[raw text](#raw-text-elements) and <a id="cdata&#45;rcdata&#45;restrictions&#58;escapable&#45;raw&#45;text&#45;elements"></a>[escapable raw text elements](#escapable-raw-text-elements) must not contain any occurrences of the string &#34;<code>&#60;&#47;</code>&#34; &#40;U&#43;003C LESS&#45;THAN SIGN&#44; U&#43;002F SOLIDUS&#41; followed by characters that case&#45;insensitively match the tag name of the element followed by one of U&#43;0009 CHARACTER TABULATION &#40;tab&#41;&#44; U&#43;000A LINE FEED &#40;LF&#41;&#44; U&#43;000C FORM FEED &#40;FF&#41;&#44; U&#43;000D CARRIAGE RETURN &#40;CR&#41;&#44; U&#43;0020 SPACE&#44; U&#43;003E GREATER&#45;THAN SIGN &#40;&#62;&#41;&#44; or U&#43;002F SOLIDUS &#40;&#47;&#41;&#46;

#### <a id="text&#45;2"></a>13&#46;1&#46;3 Text[](#text-2)

<a id="syntax&#45;text"></a><strong>Text</strong> is allowed inside elements&#44; attribute values&#44; and comments&#46; Extra constraints are placed on what is and what is not allowed in text based on where the text is to be put&#44; as described in the other sections&#46;

##### <a id="newlines"></a>13&#46;1&#46;3&#46;1 Newlines[](#newlines)

<a id="syntax&#45;newlines"></a><strong>Newlines</strong> in HTML may be represented either as U&#43;000D CARRIAGE RETURN &#40;CR&#41; characters&#44; U&#43;000A LINE FEED &#40;LF&#41; characters&#44; or pairs of U&#43;000D CARRIAGE RETURN &#40;CR&#41;&#44; U&#43;000A LINE FEED &#40;LF&#41; characters in that order&#46;

Where <a id="newlines&#58;syntax&#45;charref"></a>[character references](#syntax-charref) are allowed&#44; a character reference of a U&#43;000A LINE FEED &#40;LF&#41; character &#40;but not a U&#43;000D CARRIAGE RETURN &#40;CR&#41; character&#41; also represents a <a id="newlines&#58;syntax&#45;newlines"></a>[newline](#syntax-newlines)&#46;

#### <a id="character&#45;references"></a>13&#46;1&#46;4 Character references[](#character-references)

In certain cases described in other sections&#44; <a id="character&#45;references&#58;syntax&#45;text"></a>[text](#syntax-text) may be mixed with <a id="syntax&#45;charref"></a><strong>character references</strong>&#46; These can be used to escape characters that couldn&#39;t otherwise legally be included in <a id="character&#45;references&#58;syntax&#45;text&#45;2"></a>[text](#syntax-text)&#46;

Character references must start with a U&#43;0026 AMPERSAND character &#40;&#38;&#41;&#46; Following this&#44; there are three possible kinds of character references&#58;

<strong>Named character references</strong>

The ampersand must be followed by one of the names given in the <a id="character&#45;references&#58;named&#45;character&#45;references"></a>[named character references](#named-character-references) section&#44; using the same case&#46; The name must be one that is terminated by a U&#43;003B SEMICOLON character &#40;&#59;&#41;&#46;

<strong>Decimal numeric character reference</strong>

The ampersand must be followed by a U&#43;0023 NUMBER SIGN character &#40;&#35;&#41;&#44; followed by one or more <a id="character&#45;references&#58;ascii&#45;digits"></a>[ASCII digits](https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#ascii-digit)&#44; representing a base&#45;ten integer that corresponds to a code point that is allowed according to the definition below&#46; The digits must then be followed by a U&#43;003B SEMICOLON character &#40;&#59;&#41;&#46;

<strong>Hexadecimal numeric character reference</strong>

The ampersand must be followed by a U&#43;0023 NUMBER SIGN character &#40;&#35;&#41;&#44; which must be followed by either a U&#43;0078 LATIN SMALL LETTER X character &#40;x&#41; or a U&#43;0058 LATIN CAPITAL LETTER X character &#40;X&#41;&#44; which must then be followed by one or more <a id="character&#45;references&#58;ascii&#45;hex&#45;digits"></a>[ASCII hex digits](https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#ascii-hex-digit)&#44; representing a hexadecimal integer that corresponds to a code point that is allowed according to the definition below&#46; The digits must then be followed by a U&#43;003B SEMICOLON character &#40;&#59;&#41;&#46;

The numeric character reference forms described above are allowed to reference any code point excluding U&#43;000D CR&#44; <a id="character&#45;references&#58;noncharacter"></a>[noncharacters](https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#noncharacter)&#44; and <a id="character&#45;references&#58;control"></a>[controls](https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#control) other than <a id="character&#45;references&#58;space&#45;characters"></a>[ASCII whitespace](https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#ascii-whitespace)&#46;

An <a id="syntax&#45;ambiguous&#45;ampersand"></a><strong>ambiguous ampersand</strong> is a U&#43;0026 AMPERSAND character &#40;&#38;&#41; that is followed by one or more <a id="character&#45;references&#58;alphanumeric&#45;ascii&#45;characters"></a>[ASCII alphanumerics](https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#ascii-alphanumeric)&#44; followed by a U&#43;003B SEMICOLON character &#40;&#59;&#41;&#44; where these characters do not match any of the names given in the <a id="character&#45;references&#58;named&#45;character&#45;references&#45;2"></a>[named character references](#named-character-references) section&#46;

#### <a id="cdata&#45;sections"></a>13&#46;1&#46;5 CDATA sections[](#cdata-sections)

<a id="syntax&#45;cdata"></a><strong>CDATA sections</strong> must consist of the following components&#44; in this order&#58;

1.  The string &#34;<code>&#60;&#33;&#91;CDATA&#91;</code>&#34;&#46;
2.  Optionally&#44; <a id="cdata&#45;sections&#58;syntax&#45;text"></a>[text](#syntax-text)&#44; with the additional restriction that the text must not contain the string &#34;<code>&#93;&#93;&#62;</code>&#34;&#46;
3.  The string &#34;<code>&#93;&#93;&#62;</code>&#34;&#46;

<strong>Example&#58;</strong>

CDATA sections can only be used in foreign content &#40;MathML or SVG&#41;&#46; In this example&#44; a CDATA section is used to escape the contents of a <a id="cdata&#45;sections&#58;mathml&#45;ms"></a>[MathML <code>ms</code>](https://w3c.github.io/mathml-core/#string-literal-ms) element&#58;

``` text
<p>You can add a string to a number, but this stringifies the number:</p>
<math>
 <ms><![CDATA[x<y]]></ms>
 <mo>+</mo>
 <mn>3</mn>
 <mo>=</mo>
 <ms><![CDATA[x<y3]]></ms>
</math>
```

#### <a id="comments"></a>13&#46;1&#46;6 Comments[](#comments)

<a id="syntax&#45;comments"></a><strong>Comments</strong> must have the following format&#58;

1.  The string &#34;<code>&#60;&#33;&#45;&#45;</code>&#34;&#46;
2.  Optionally&#44; <a id="comments&#58;syntax&#45;text"></a>[text](#syntax-text)&#44; with the additional restriction that the text must not start with the string &#34;<code>&#62;</code>&#34;&#44; nor start with the string &#34;<code>&#45;&#62;</code>&#34;&#44; nor contain the strings &#34;<code>&#60;&#33;&#45;&#45;</code>&#34;&#44; &#34;<code>&#45;&#45;&#62;</code>&#34;&#44; or &#34;<code>&#45;&#45;&#33;&#62;</code>&#34;&#44; nor end with the string &#34;<code>&#60;&#33;&#45;</code>&#34;&#46;
3.  The string &#34;<code>&#45;&#45;&#62;</code>&#34;&#46;

<strong>Note&#58;</strong>

The <a id="comments&#58;syntax&#45;text&#45;2"></a>[text](#syntax-text) is allowed to end with the string &#34;<code>&#60;&#33;</code>&#34;&#44; as in <code>&#60;&#33;&#45;&#45;My favorite operators are &#62; and &#60;&#33;&#45;&#45;&#62;</code>&#46;

#### <a id="processing&#45;instructions"></a>13&#46;1&#46;7 Processing instructions[](#processing-instructions)

A processing instruction marks a location in a document for further processing&#46;

<a id="syntax&#45;processing&#45;instruction"></a><strong>Processing instructions</strong> must have the following format&#58;

1.  &#34;<code>&#60;&#63;</code>&#34;&#46;

2.  A <a id="processing&#45;instructions&#58;syntax&#45;pi&#45;target"></a>[target](#syntax-pi-target)&#46;

3.  Either of the following two options&#58;

    - Zero or more <a id="processing&#45;instructions&#58;space&#45;characters"></a>[ASCII whitespace](https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#ascii-whitespace)&#46;
    - One or more <a id="processing&#45;instructions&#58;space&#45;characters&#45;2"></a>[ASCII whitespace](https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#ascii-whitespace)&#44; followed by <a id="processing&#45;instructions&#58;syntax&#45;pi&#45;data"></a>[data](#syntax-pi-data)&#46;

4.  Optionally&#44; a U&#43;003F &#40;&#63;&#41;&#46;

5.  A U&#43;003E &#40;&#62;&#41;&#46;

The <a id="syntax&#45;pi&#45;target"></a><strong>target</strong> consists of <a id="processing&#45;instructions&#58;alphanumeric&#45;ascii&#45;characters"></a>[ASCII alphanumeric](https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#ascii-alphanumeric)&#44; U&#43;002D &#40;&#45;&#41;&#44; and U&#43;005F &#40;&#95;&#41; code points&#46; It must start with an <a id="processing&#45;instructions&#58;ascii&#45;letters"></a>[ASCII alpha](https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#ascii-alpha) or U&#43;005F &#40;&#95;&#41; and must not be an <a id="processing&#45;instructions&#58;ascii&#45;case&#45;insensitive"></a>[ASCII case&#45;insensitive](https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#ascii-case-insensitive) match for &#34;<code>xml</code>&#34; or &#34;<code>xml&#45;stylesheet</code>&#34;&#46;

The <a id="syntax&#45;pi&#45;data"></a><strong>data</strong> is <a id="processing&#45;instructions&#58;syntax&#45;text"></a>[text](#syntax-text)&#44; with the additional restriction that the text must not contain U&#43;003E &#40;&#62;&#41;&#44; nor end with U&#43;003F &#40;&#63;&#41;&#46;

<strong>Note&#58;</strong>

Processing instructions in the HTML syntax have some notable differences to [processing instructions in XML](https://www.w3.org/TR/xml/#sec-pi)&#58; [&#91;XML&#93;](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/commit-snapshots/877d6146487f15b15bc8dd0e3c625063a37b456a/#refsXML)

- In HTML&#44; a processing instruction can end with &#34;<code>&#62;</code>&#34; or &#34;<code>&#63;&#62;</code>&#34;&#44; while in XML it can only end with &#34;<code>&#63;&#62;</code>&#34;&#46;

- In HTML&#44; &#34;<code>&#60;&#63;xml &#46;&#46;&#46;&#63;&#62;</code>&#34; and &#34;<code>&#60;&#63;xml&#45;stylesheet &#46;&#46;&#46;&#63;&#62;</code>&#34; specifically are not parsed as processing instructions but instead treated as <a id="processing&#45;instructions&#58;bogus&#45;comment&#45;state"></a>[bogus comments](#bogus-comment-state)&#46; This is for compatibility with existing HTML content&#44; where such syntax is relatively common&#46;

- HTML does not support the full [Name](https://www.w3.org/TR/xml/#NT-Name) production for <a id="processing&#45;instructions&#58;syntax&#45;pi&#45;target&#45;2"></a>[processing instruction targets](#syntax-pi-target)&#46; A much more limited subset is allowed&#44; as noted above&#46; [&#91;XML&#93;](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/commit-snapshots/877d6146487f15b15bc8dd0e3c625063a37b456a/#refsXML)

### <a id="parsing"></a>13&#46;2 Parsing HTML documents[](#parsing)

<em>This section only applies to user agents&#44; data mining tools&#44; and conformance checkers&#46;</em>

<strong>Note&#58;</strong>

The rules for parsing XML documents into DOM trees are covered by the next section&#44; entitled &#34;<a id="parsing&#58;the&#45;xhtml&#45;syntax"></a>[The XML syntax](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/commit-snapshots/877d6146487f15b15bc8dd0e3c625063a37b456a/#the-xhtml-syntax)&#34;&#46;

User agents must use the parsing rules described in this section to generate the DOM trees from <a id="parsing&#58;text&#47;html"></a><code>[text&#47;html](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/commit-snapshots/877d6146487f15b15bc8dd0e3c625063a37b456a/#text/html)</code> resources&#46; Together&#44; these rules define what is referred to as the <a id="html&#45;parser"></a><strong>HTML parser</strong>&#46;

<strong>Note&#58;</strong>

While the HTML syntax described in this specification bears a close resemblance to SGML and XML&#44; it is a separate language with its own parsing rules&#46;

Some earlier versions of HTML &#40;in particular from HTML2 to HTML4&#41; were based on SGML and used SGML parsing rules&#46; However&#44; few &#40;if any&#41; web browsers ever implemented true SGML parsing for HTML documents&#59; the only user agents to strictly handle HTML as an SGML application have historically been validators&#46; The resulting confusion — with validators claiming documents to have one representation while widely deployed web browsers interoperably implemented a different representation — has wasted decades of productivity&#46; This version of HTML thus returns to a non&#45;SGML basis&#46;

For the purposes of conformance checkers&#44; if a resource is determined to be in <a id="parsing&#58;syntax"></a>[the HTML syntax](#syntax)&#44; then it is an <a id="parsing&#58;html&#45;documents"></a>[HTML document](https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#html-document)&#46;

<strong>Note&#58;</strong>

As stated <a id="parsing&#58;html&#45;elements"></a>[in the terminology section](html-language-foundations--877d6146487f--b55e73c31978.md#html-elements)&#44; references to <a id="parsing&#58;element&#45;type"></a>[element types](html-language-foundations--877d6146487f--b55e73c31978.md#element-type) that do not explicitly specify a namespace always refer to elements in the <a id="parsing&#58;html&#45;namespace&#45;2"></a>[HTML namespace](https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#html-namespace)&#46; For example&#44; if the spec talks about &#34;a <a id="parsing&#58;the&#45;menu&#45;element"></a><code>[menu](html-language-elements-text-links--877d6146487f--8833a85fd242.md#the-menu-element)</code> element&#34;&#44; then that is an element with the local name &#34;<code>menu</code>&#34;&#44; the namespace &#34;<code>http&#58;&#47;&#47;www&#46;w3&#46;org&#47;1999&#47;xhtml</code>&#34;&#44; and the interface <a id="parsing&#58;htmlmenuelement"></a><code>[HTMLMenuElement](html-language-elements-text-links--877d6146487f--8833a85fd242.md#htmlmenuelement)</code>&#46; Where possible&#44; references to such elements are hyperlinked to their definition&#46;

#### <a id="overview&#45;of&#45;the&#45;parsing&#45;model"></a>13&#46;2&#46;1 Overview of the parsing model[](#overview-of-the-parsing-model)

![](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/images/parsing-model-overview.svg)

The input to the HTML parsing process consists of a stream of <a id="overview&#45;of&#45;the&#45;parsing&#45;model&#58;code&#45;point"></a>[code points](https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#code-point)&#44; which is passed through a <a id="overview&#45;of&#45;the&#45;parsing&#45;model&#58;tokenization"></a>[tokenization](#tokenization) stage followed by a <a id="overview&#45;of&#45;the&#45;parsing&#45;model&#58;tree&#45;construction"></a>[tree construction](#tree-construction) stage&#46; The output is a <a id="overview&#45;of&#45;the&#45;parsing&#45;model&#58;document"></a><code>[Document](html-language-foundations--877d6146487f--b55e73c31978.md#document)</code> object&#46;

<strong>Note&#58;</strong>

Implementations that [do not support scripting](html-language-foundations--877d6146487f--b55e73c31978.md#non-scripted) do not have to actually create a DOM <a id="overview&#45;of&#45;the&#45;parsing&#45;model&#58;document&#45;2"></a><code>[Document](html-language-foundations--877d6146487f--b55e73c31978.md#document)</code> object&#44; but the DOM tree in such cases is still used as the model for the rest of the specification&#46;

In the common case&#44; the data handled by the tokenization stage comes from the network&#44; but <a id="overview&#45;of&#45;the&#45;parsing&#45;model&#58;dynamic&#45;markup&#45;insertion"></a>[it can also come from script](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/commit-snapshots/877d6146487f15b15bc8dd0e3c625063a37b456a/#dynamic-markup-insertion) running in the user agent&#44; e&#46;g&#46; using the <a id="overview&#45;of&#45;the&#45;parsing&#45;model&#58;dom&#45;document&#45;write"></a><code>[document&#46;write&#40;&#41;](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/commit-snapshots/877d6146487f15b15bc8dd0e3c625063a37b456a/#dom-document-write)</code> API&#46;

<a id="nestedParsing"></a>There is only one set of states for the tokenizer stage and the tree construction stage&#44; but the tree construction stage is reentrant&#44; meaning that while the tree construction stage is handling one token&#44; the tokenizer might be resumed&#44; causing further tokens to be emitted and processed before the first token&#39;s processing is complete&#46;

<strong>Example&#58;</strong>

In the following example&#44; the tree construction stage will be called upon to handle a &#34;p&#34; start tag token while handling the &#34;script&#34; end tag token&#58;

``` text
...
<script>
 document.write('<p>');
</script>
...
```

To handle these cases&#44; parsers have a <a id="script&#45;nesting&#45;level"></a><strong>script nesting level</strong>&#44; which must be initially set to zero&#44; and a <a id="parser&#45;pause&#45;flag"></a><strong>parser pause flag</strong>&#44; which must be initially set to false&#46;

#### <a id="parse&#45;errors"></a>13&#46;2&#46;2 <strong>Parse errors</strong>[](#parse-errors)

This specification defines the parsing rules for HTML documents&#44; whether they are syntactically correct or not&#46; Certain points in the parsing algorithm are said to be <a id="parse&#45;errors&#58;parse&#45;errors"></a>[parse errors](#parse-errors)&#46; The error handling for parse errors is well&#45;defined &#40;that&#39;s the processing rules described throughout this specification&#41;&#44; but user agents&#44; while parsing an HTML document&#44; may <a id="parse&#45;errors&#58;abort&#45;a&#45;parser"></a>[abort the parser](#abort-a-parser) at the first <a id="parse&#45;errors&#58;parse&#45;errors&#45;2"></a>[parse error](#parse-errors) that they encounter for which they do not wish to apply the rules described in this specification&#46;

Conformance checkers must report at least one parse error condition to the user if one or more parse error conditions exist in the document and must not report parse error conditions if none exist in the document&#46; Conformance checkers may report more than one parse error condition if more than one parse error condition exists in the document&#46;

<strong>Note&#58;</strong>

Parse errors are only errors with the <em>syntax</em> of HTML&#46; In addition to checking for parse errors&#44; conformance checkers will also verify that the document obeys all the other conformance requirements described in this specification&#46;

Some parse errors have dedicated codes outlined in the table below that should be used by conformance checkers in reports&#46;

<em>Error descriptions in the table below are non&#45;normative&#46;</em>

<table class="parse-error-table"><thead><tr><th>Code      </th><th>Description     </th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td><dfn id="parse-error-abrupt-closing-of-empty-comment">abrupt&#45;closing&#45;of&#45;empty&#45;comment</dfn>      </td><td><p>This error occurs if the parser encounters an empty <a href="#syntax-comments" id="parse-errors:syntax-comments">comment</a> that is abruptly closed by a U&#43;003E &#40;&gt;&#41; <a id="parse-errors:code-point-2" href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#code-point" data-x-internal="code-point">code point</a> in the      <a href="#syntax-doctype" id="parse-errors:syntax-doctype">DOCTYPE</a> public identifier &#40;e&#46;g&#46;&#44; In this case the parser treats the beginning of a <a href="#syntax-start-tag" id="parse-errors:syntax-start-tag">start tag</a> &#40;i&#46;e&#46;&#44; <code>&lt;</code>&#41; or an <a href="#syntax-end-tag" id="parse-errors:syntax-end-tag-3">end tag</a> &#40;i&#46;e&#46;&#44; <code>&lt;&#47;</code>&#41; as text      content&#46;</p>      </td></tr><tr><td><dfn id="parse-error-eof-in-cdata">eof&#45;in&#45;cdata</dfn>      </td><td><p>This error occurs if the parser encounters the end of the <a href="#input-stream" id="parse-errors:input-stream-4">input stream</a> in a      <a href="#syntax-cdata" id="parse-errors:syntax-cdata-2">CDATA section</a>&#46; The parser treats such CDATA sections as if      they are closed immediately before the end of the input stream&#46;</p>      </td></tr><tr><td><dfn id="parse-error-eof-in-comment">eof&#45;in&#45;comment</dfn>      </td><td><p>This error occurs if the parser encounters the end of the <a href="#input-stream" id="parse-errors:input-stream-5">input stream</a> in a      <a href="#syntax-comments" id="parse-errors:syntax-comments-2">comment</a>&#46; The parser treats such comments as if they are      closed immediately before the end of the input stream&#46;</p>      </td></tr><tr><td><dfn id="parse-error-eof-in-doctype">eof&#45;in&#45;doctype</dfn>      </td><td><p>This error occurs if the parser encounters the end of the input stream in a <a href="#syntax-doctype" id="parse-errors:syntax-doctype-3">DOCTYPE</a>&#46; In such a case&#44; if the DOCTYPE is correctly placed as a      document preamble&#44; the parser sets the <code id="parse-errors:document-3"><a href="html-language-foundations--877d6146487f--b55e73c31978.md#document">Document</a></code> to <a id="parse-errors:quirks-mode-3" href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-document-quirks" data-x-internal="quirks-mode">quirks mode</a>&#46;</p>      </td></tr><tr><td><dfn id="parse-error-eof-in-processing-instruction">eof&#45;in&#45;processing&#45;instruction</dfn>      </td><td><p>This error occurs if the parser encounters the end of the <a href="#input-stream" id="parse-errors:input-stream-6">input stream</a> in a      <a href="#syntax-processing-instruction" id="parse-errors:syntax-processing-instruction">processing instruction</a> &#40;e&#46;g&#46;&#44; <code>&lt;&#63;</code> or <code>&lt;&#63;marker name&#61;</code>&#41;&#46; Such processing      instructions are ignored&#46;</p>      </td></tr><tr><td><dfn id="parse-error-eof-in-script-html-comment-like-text">eof&#45;in&#45;script&#45;html&#45;comment&#45;like&#45;text</dfn>      </td><td>       <p>This error occurs if the parser encounters the end of the <a href="#input-stream" id="parse-errors:input-stream-7">input stream</a> in text       that resembles an <a href="#syntax-comments" id="parse-errors:syntax-comments-3">HTML comment</a> inside       <code id="parse-errors:the-script-element"><a href="html-language-elements-interactive-scripting--877d6146487f--05bb1d85cc89.md#the-script-element">script</a></code> element content &#40;e&#46;g&#46;&#44; <code>&lt;script&gt;&lt;&#33;&#45;&#45; foo</code>&#41;&#46;</p>        <p class="note">Syntactic structures that resemble HTML comments in <code id="parse-errors:the-script-element-2"><a href="html-language-elements-interactive-scripting--877d6146487f--05bb1d85cc89.md#the-script-element">script</a></code>       elements are parsed as text content&#46; They can be a part of a scripting language&#45;specific       syntactic structure or be treated as an HTML&#45;like comment&#44; if the scripting language supports       them &#40;e&#46;g&#46;&#44; parsing rules for HTML&#45;like comments can be found in Annex B of the JavaScript       specification&#41;&#46; The common reason for this error is a violation of the <a href="html-language-elements-interactive-scripting--877d6146487f--05bb1d85cc89.md#restrictions-for-contents-of-script-elements" id="parse-errors:restrictions-for-contents-of-script-elements">restrictions for contents of <code>script</code> elements</a>&#46; <a href="https://html.spec.whatwg.org/commit-snapshots/877d6146487f15b15bc8dd0e3c625063a37b456a/#refsJAVASCRIPT">&#91;JAVASCRIPT&#93;</a></p>      </td></tr><tr><td><dfn id="parse-error-eof-in-tag">eof&#45;in&#45;tag</dfn>      </td><td><p>This error occurs if the parser encounters the end of the <a href="#input-stream" id="parse-errors:input-stream-8">input stream</a> in a      <a href="#syntax-start-tag" id="parse-errors:syntax-start-tag-2">start tag</a> or an <a href="#syntax-end-tag" id="parse-errors:syntax-end-tag-4">end      tag</a> &#40;e&#46;g&#46;&#44; <code>&lt;div id&#61;</code>&#41;&#46; Such a tag is ignored&#46;</p>      </td></tr><tr><td><dfn id="parse-error-incorrectly-closed-comment">incorrectly&#45;closed&#45;comment</dfn>      </td><td><p>This error occurs if the parser encounters a <a href="#syntax-comments" id="parse-errors:syntax-comments-4">comment</a> that is closed by the &#34;<code>&#45;&#45;&#33;&gt;</code>&#34;      <a id="parse-errors:code-point-8" href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#code-point" data-x-internal="code-point">code point</a> sequence&#46; The parser treats such comments as if they are correctly      closed by the &#34;<code>&#45;&#45;&gt;</code>&#34; code point sequence&#46;</p>      </td></tr><tr><td><dfn id="parse-error-incorrectly-opened-comment">incorrectly&#45;opened&#45;comment</dfn>      </td><td>       <p>This error occurs if the parser encounters the &#34;<code>&lt;&#33;</code>&#34; <a id="parse-errors:code-point-9" href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#code-point" data-x-internal="code-point">code       point</a> sequence that is not immediately followed by two U&#43;002D &#40;&#45;&#41; code points and that       is not the start of a <a href="#syntax-doctype" id="parse-errors:syntax-doctype-4">DOCTYPE</a> or a <a href="#syntax-cdata" id="parse-errors:syntax-cdata-3">CDATA section</a>&#46; All content that follows the &#34;<code>&lt;&#33;</code>&#34; code point sequence up to a U&#43;003E &#40;&gt;&#41; code point &#40;if present&#41; or to       the end of the <a href="#input-stream" id="parse-errors:input-stream-9">input stream</a> is treated as a comment&#46;</p>        <p class="note">One possible cause of this error is using an XML markup declaration &#40;e&#46;g&#46;&#44;       <code>&lt;&#33;ELEMENT br EMPTY&gt;</code>&#41; in HTML&#46;</p>      </td></tr><tr><td><dfn id="parse-error-invalid-character-sequence-after-doctype-name">invalid&#45;character&#45;sequence&#45;after&#45;doctype&#45;name</dfn>      </td><td><p>This error occurs if the parser encounters any <a id="parse-errors:code-point-10" href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#code-point" data-x-internal="code-point">code point</a> sequence other      than &#34;<code>PUBLIC</code>&#34; and &#34;<code>SYSTEM</code>&#34; keywords after a <a href="#syntax-doctype" id="parse-errors:syntax-doctype-5">DOCTYPE</a> name&#46; In such a case&#44; the parser ignores any following      public or system identifiers&#44; and if the DOCTYPE is correctly placed as a document preamble&#44;      and if the <a href="#parser-cannot-change-the-mode-flag" id="parse-errors:parser-cannot-change-the-mode-flag">parser cannot change the mode flag</a> is false&#44; sets the <code id="parse-errors:document-4"><a href="html-language-foundations--877d6146487f--b55e73c31978.md#document">Document</a></code>      to <a id="parse-errors:quirks-mode-4" href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-document-quirks" data-x-internal="quirks-mode">quirks mode</a>&#46;</p>      </td></tr><tr><td><dfn id="parse-error-invalid-first-character-of-processing-instruction-target">invalid&#45;first&#45;character&#45;of&#45;processing&#45;instruction&#45;target</dfn>      </td><td>       <p>This error occurs if the parser encounters a <a id="parse-errors:code-point-11" href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#code-point" data-x-internal="code-point">code point</a> that is not an       <a id="parse-errors:ascii-letters" href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#ascii-alpha" data-x-internal="ascii-letters">ASCII alpha</a> or U&#43;005F &#40;&#95;&#41; where the first code point of a <a href="#syntax-pi-target" id="parse-errors:syntax-pi-target-2">processing instruction target</a> is expected&#46; The preceding       U&#43;003F &#40;&#63;&#41; and all content that follows up to a U&#43;003E &#40;&gt;&#41; &#40;if present&#41; or to the end of the       <a href="#input-stream" id="parse-errors:input-stream-10">input stream</a> is treated as a comment&#46;</p>      </td></tr><tr><td><dfn id="parse-error-invalid-first-character-of-tag-name">invalid&#45;first&#45;character&#45;of&#45;tag&#45;name</dfn>      </td><td>       <p>This error occurs if the parser encounters a <a id="parse-errors:code-point-12" href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#code-point" data-x-internal="code-point">code point</a> that is not an       <a id="parse-errors:ascii-letters-2" href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#ascii-alpha" data-x-internal="ascii-letters">ASCII alpha</a> where the first code point of a <a href="#syntax-start-tag" id="parse-errors:syntax-start-tag-3">start       tag</a> name or an <a href="#syntax-end-tag" id="parse-errors:syntax-end-tag-5">end tag</a> name is expected&#46; If a       start tag was expected such code point and a preceding U&#43;003C &#40;&lt;&#41; is treated as text       content&#44; and all content that follows is treated as markup&#46; Whereas&#44; if an end tag was       expected&#44; such code point and all content that follows up to a U&#43;003E &#40;&gt;&#41; code point &#40;if       present&#41; or to the end of the <a href="#input-stream" id="parse-errors:input-stream-11">input stream</a> is treated as a comment&#46;</p>        <div class="example">        <p>For example&#44; consider the following markup&#58;</p>         <code>&lt;42&gt;&lt;&#47;42&gt;</code>         <p>This will be parsed into&#58;</p>         <ul class="domTree"><li class="t1"><code id="parse-errors:the-html-element"><a href="html-language-elements-attributes--877d6146487f--2ca83b5ac984.md#the-html-element">html</a></code><ul><li class="t1"><code id="parse-errors:the-head-element"><a href="html-language-elements-attributes--877d6146487f--2ca83b5ac984.md#the-head-element">head</a></code></li><li class="t1"><code id="parse-errors:the-body-element"><a href="html-language-elements-text-links--877d6146487f--8833a85fd242.md#the-body-element">body</a></code><ul><li class="t3"><code id="parse-errors:text"><a data-x-internal="text" href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#interface-text">&#35;text</a></code>&#58; <span>&lt;42&gt;</span></li><li class="t8"><code id="parse-errors:comment-2"><a data-x-internal="comment-2" href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#interface-comment">&#35;comment</a></code>&#58; <span>42</span></li></ul></li></ul></li></ul>       </div>        <p class="note">While the first code point of a tag name is limited to an <a id="parse-errors:ascii-letters-3" href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#ascii-alpha" data-x-internal="ascii-letters">ASCII       alpha</a>&#44; a wide range of code points &#40;including <a id="parse-errors:ascii-digits" href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#ascii-digit" data-x-internal="ascii-digits">ASCII digits</a>&#41; is allowed in       subsequent positions&#46;</p>      </td></tr><tr><td><dfn id="parse-error-invalid-processing-instruction-target">invalid&#45;processing&#45;instruction&#45;target</dfn>      </td><td>       <p>This error occurs if the parser encounters a <a id="parse-errors:code-point-13" href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#code-point" data-x-internal="code-point">code point</a> that is not an       <a id="parse-errors:alphanumeric-ascii-characters" href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#ascii-alphanumeric" data-x-internal="alphanumeric-ascii-characters">ASCII alphanumeric</a>&#44; U&#43;002D &#40;&#45;&#41;&#44; or U&#43;005F &#40;&#95;&#41; where a <a href="#syntax-pi-target" id="parse-errors:syntax-pi-target-3">processing instruction target</a> is expected&#46; The preceding       U&#43;003F &#40;&#63;&#41; and all content that follows up to a U&#43;003E &#40;&gt;&#41; &#40;if present&#41; or to the end of the       <a href="#input-stream" id="parse-errors:input-stream-12">input stream</a> is treated as a comment&#46;</p>      </td></tr><tr><td><dfn id="parse-error-missing-attribute-value">missing&#45;attribute&#45;value</dfn>      </td><td><p>This error occurs if the parser encounters a U&#43;003E &#40;&gt;&#41; <a id="parse-errors:code-point-14" href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#code-point" data-x-internal="code-point">code point</a> where an      <a href="#syntax-attributes" id="parse-errors:syntax-attributes-3">attribute</a> value is expected &#40;e&#46;g&#46;&#44; <code>&lt;div id&#61;&gt;</code>&#41;&#46; The parser treats the attribute as having an empty value&#46;</p>      </td></tr><tr><td><dfn id="parse-error-missing-doctype-name">missing&#45;doctype&#45;name</dfn>      </td><td><p>This error occurs if the parser encounters a <a href="#syntax-doctype" id="parse-errors:syntax-doctype-6">DOCTYPE</a> that is missing a name &#40;e&#46;g&#46;&#44; <code>&lt;&#33;DOCTYPE&gt;</code>&#41;&#46; In such a case&#44; if the DOCTYPE is correctly placed as a      document preamble&#44; the parser sets the <code id="parse-errors:document-5"><a href="html-language-foundations--877d6146487f--b55e73c31978.md#document">Document</a></code> to <a id="parse-errors:quirks-mode-5" href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-document-quirks" data-x-internal="quirks-mode">quirks mode</a>&#46;</p>      </td></tr><tr><td><dfn id="parse-error-missing-doctype-public-identifier">missing&#45;doctype&#45;public&#45;identifier</dfn>      </td><td><p>This error occurs if the parser encounters a U&#43;003E &#40;&gt;&#41; <a id="parse-errors:code-point-15" href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#code-point" data-x-internal="code-point">code point</a> where      start of the <a href="#syntax-doctype" id="parse-errors:syntax-doctype-7">DOCTYPE</a> public identifier is expected &#40;e&#46;g&#46;&#44;      <code>&lt;&#33;DOCTYPE html PUBLIC &gt;</code>&#41;&#46; In such a case&#44; if the DOCTYPE is correctly      placed as a document preamble&#44; the parser sets the <code id="parse-errors:document-6"><a href="html-language-foundations--877d6146487f--b55e73c31978.md#document">Document</a></code> to <a id="parse-errors:quirks-mode-6" href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-document-quirks" data-x-internal="quirks-mode">quirks      mode</a>&#46;</p>      </td></tr><tr><td><dfn id="parse-error-missing-doctype-system-identifier">missing&#45;doctype&#45;system&#45;identifier</dfn>      </td><td><p>This error occurs if the parser encounters a U&#43;003E &#40;&gt;&#41; <a id="parse-errors:code-point-16" href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#code-point" data-x-internal="code-point">code point</a> where      start of the <a href="#syntax-doctype" id="parse-errors:syntax-doctype-8">DOCTYPE</a> system identifier is expected &#40;e&#46;g&#46;&#44;      <code>&lt;&#33;DOCTYPE html SYSTEM &gt;</code>&#41;&#46; In such a case&#44; if the DOCTYPE is correctly      placed as a document preamble&#44; the parser sets the <code id="parse-errors:document-7"><a href="html-language-foundations--877d6146487f--b55e73c31978.md#document">Document</a></code> to <a id="parse-errors:quirks-mode-7" href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-document-quirks" data-x-internal="quirks-mode">quirks      mode</a>&#46;</p>      </td></tr><tr><td><dfn id="parse-error-missing-end-tag-name">missing&#45;end&#45;tag&#45;name</dfn>      </td><td><p>This error occurs if the parser encounters a U&#43;003E &#40;&gt;&#41; <a id="parse-errors:code-point-17" href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#code-point" data-x-internal="code-point">code point</a> where an      <a href="#syntax-end-tag" id="parse-errors:syntax-end-tag-6">end tag</a> name is expected&#44; i&#46;e&#46;&#44; <code>&lt;&#47;&gt;</code>&#46; The parser ignores the whole &#34;<code>&lt;&#47;&gt;</code>&#34; code      point sequence&#46;</p>      </td></tr><tr><td><dfn id="parse-error-missing-quote-before-doctype-public-identifier">missing&#45;quote&#45;before&#45;doctype&#45;public&#45;identifier</dfn>      </td><td><p>This error occurs if the parser encounters the <a href="#syntax-doctype" id="parse-errors:syntax-doctype-9">DOCTYPE</a> public identifier that is not preceded by a quote &#40;e&#46;g&#46;&#44;      <code>&lt;&#33;DOCTYPE html PUBLIC &#45;&#47;&#47;W3C&#47;&#47;DTD HTML 4&#46;01&#47;&#47;EN&#34;&gt;</code>&#41;&#46; In such a case&#44;      the parser ignores the public identifier&#44; and if the DOCTYPE is correctly placed as a document      preamble&#44; sets the <code id="parse-errors:document-8"><a href="html-language-foundations--877d6146487f--b55e73c31978.md#document">Document</a></code> to <a id="parse-errors:quirks-mode-8" href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-document-quirks" data-x-internal="quirks-mode">quirks mode</a>&#46;</p>      </td></tr><tr><td><dfn id="parse-error-missing-quote-before-doctype-system-identifier">missing&#45;quote&#45;before&#45;doctype&#45;system&#45;identifier</dfn>      </td><td><p>This error occurs if the parser encounters the <a href="#syntax-doctype" id="parse-errors:syntax-doctype-10">DOCTYPE</a> system identifier that is not preceded by a quote &#40;e&#46;g&#46;&#44;      <code>&lt;&#33;DOCTYPE html SYSTEM&#10;     http&#58;&#47;&#47;www&#46;w3&#46;org&#47;TR&#47;xhtml1&#47;DTD&#47;xhtml1&#45;transitional&#46;dtd&#34;&gt;</code>&#41;&#46; In such a case&#44; the parser      ignores the system identifier&#44; and if the DOCTYPE is correctly placed as a document preamble&#44;      sets the <code id="parse-errors:document-9"><a href="html-language-foundations--877d6146487f--b55e73c31978.md#document">Document</a></code> to <a id="parse-errors:quirks-mode-9" href="https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-document-quirks" data-x-internal="quirks-mode">quirks mode</a>&#46;</p>      </td></tr><tr><td><dfn id="parse-error-missing-semicolon-after-character-reference">missing&#45;semicolon&#45;after&#45;character&#45;reference</dfn>      </td><td>       <p>This error occurs if the parser encounters a <a href="#syntax-charref" id="parse-errors:syntax-charref-4">character       reference</a> that is not terminated by a U&#43;003B &#40;&#59;&#41; <a id="parse-errors:code-point-18" href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#code-point" data-x-internal="code-point">code point</a>&#46;       The parser behaves the same as if the character reference is terminated by the U&#43;003B       &#40;&#59;&#41; code point&#46;</p>        <p class="note">Most <a href="#named-character-references" id="parse-errors:named-character-references">named character references</a> require a terminating U&#43;003B       &#40;&#59;&#41; <a id="parse-errors:code-point-19" href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#code-point" data-x-internal="code-point">code point</a>&#46; Those that don&#39;t might get resolved as a longer named <a href="#syntax-charref" id="parse-errors:syntax-charref-5">character reference</a> in certain ambiguous scenarios&#46;</p>        <p class="example">For example&#44; <code>&amp;notin</code> will be parsed as &#34;<code>¬in</code>&#34;&#44; i&#46;e&#46;&#44; the same as if the input were <code>&amp;not&#59;in</code>&#44; whereas <code>&amp;notin&#59;</code> will be parsed as       &#34;<code>∉</code>&#34;&#46;</p>      </td></tr><tr><td><dfn id="parse-error-missing-whitespace-after-doctype-public-keyword">missing&#45;whitespace&#45;after&#45;doctype&#45;public&#45;keyword</dfn>      </td><td><p>This error occurs if the parser encounters a <a href="#syntax-doctype" id="parse-errors:syntax-doctype-11">DOCTYPE</a> whose &#34;<code>PUBLIC</code>&#34; keyword and public      identifier are not separated by <a id="parse-errors:space-characters-3" href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#ascii-whitespace" data-x-internal="space-characters">ASCII whitespace</a>&#46; In this case the parser behaves      as if ASCII whitespace is present&#46;</p>      </td></tr><tr><td><dfn id="parse-error-missing-whitespace-after-doctype-system-keyword">missing&#45;whitespace&#45;after&#45;doctype&#45;system&#45;keyword</dfn>      </td><td><p>This error occurs if the parser encounters a <a href="#syntax-doctype" id="parse-errors:syntax-doctype-12">DOCTYPE</a> whose &#34;<code>SYSTEM</code>&#34; keyword and system      identifier are not separated by <a id="parse-errors:space-characters-4" href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#ascii-whitespace" data-x-internal="space-characters">ASCII whitespace</a>&#46; In this case the parser behaves      as if ASCII whitespace is present&#46;</p>      </td></tr><tr><td><dfn id="parse-error-missing-whitespace-before-doctype-name">missing&#45;whitespace&#45;before&#45;doctype&#45;name</dfn>      </td><td><p>This error occurs if the parser encounters a <a href="#syntax-doctype" id="parse-errors:syntax-doctype-13">DOCTYPE</a> whose &#34;<code>DOCTYPE</code>&#34; keyword and name      are not separated by <a id="parse-errors:space-characters-5" href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#ascii-whitespace" data-x-internal="space-characters">ASCII whitespace</a>&#46; In this case the parser behaves as if ASCII      whitespace is present&#46;</p>      </td></tr><tr><td><dfn id="parse-error-missing-whitespace-between-attributes">missing&#45;whitespace&#45;between&#45;attributes</dfn>      </td><td><p>This error occurs if the parser encounters <a href="#syntax-attributes" id="parse-errors:syntax-attributes-4">attributes</a> that are not separated by <a id="parse-errors:space-characters-6" href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#ascii-whitespace" data-x-internal="space-characters">ASCII      whitespace</a> &#40;e&#46;g&#46;&#44; <code>&lt;div id&#61;&#34;foo&#34;class&#61;&#34;bar&#34;&gt;</code>&#41;&#46; In this case the      parser behaves as if ASCII whitespace is present&#46;</p>      </td></tr><tr><td><dfn id="parse-error-missing-whitespace-between-doctype-public-and-system-identifiers">missing&#45;whitespace&#45;between&#45;doctype&#45;public&#45;and&#45;system&#45;identifiers</dfn>      </td><td><p>This error occurs if the parser encounters a <a href="#syntax-doctype" id="parse-errors:syntax-doctype-14">DOCTYPE</a> whose public and system identifiers are not separated by      <a id="parse-errors:space-characters-7" href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#ascii-whitespace" data-x-internal="space-characters">ASCII whitespace</a>&#46; In this case the parser behaves as if ASCII whitespace is      present&#46;</p>      </td></tr><tr><td><dfn id="parse-error-nested-comment">nested&#45;comment</dfn>      </td><td><p>This error occurs if the parser encounters a nested <a href="#syntax-comments" id="parse-errors:syntax-comments-5">comment</a> &#40;e&#46;g&#46;&#44; <code>&lt;&#33;&#45;&#45; &lt;&#33;&#45;&#45; nested &#45;&#45;&gt;&#10;     &#45;&#45;&gt;</code>&#41;&#46; Such a comment will be closed by the first occurring &#34;<code>&#45;&#45;&gt;</code>&#34;      <a id="parse-errors:code-point-20" href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#code-point" data-x-internal="code-point">code point</a> sequence and everything that follows will be treated as markup&#46;</p>      </td></tr><tr><td><dfn id="parse-error-noncharacter-character-reference">noncharacter&#45;character&#45;reference</dfn>      </td><td><p>This error occurs if the parser encounters a numeric <a href="#syntax-charref" id="parse-errors:syntax-charref-6">character reference</a> that references a <a id="parse-errors:noncharacter" href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#noncharacter" data-x-internal="noncharacter">noncharacter</a>&#46;      The parser resolves such character references as&#45;is&#46;</p>      </td></tr><tr><td><dfn id="parse-error-noncharacter-in-input-stream">noncharacter&#45;in&#45;input&#45;stream</dfn>      </td><td><p>This error occurs if the <a href="#input-stream" id="parse-errors:input-stream-13">input stream</a> contains a <a id="parse-errors:noncharacter-2" href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#noncharacter" data-x-internal="noncharacter">noncharacter</a>&#46;      Such <a href="https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#code-point" id="parse-errors:code-point-21" data-x-internal="code-point">code points</a> are parsed as&#45;is and usually&#44; where parsing      rules don&#39;t apply any additional restrictions&#44; #### <a id="the&#45;input&#45;byte&#45;stream"></a>13&#46;2&#46;3 The <strong>input byte stream</strong>[](#the-input-byte-stream)

The stream of code points that comprises the input to the tokenization stage will be initially seen by the user agent as a stream of bytes &#40;typically coming over the network or from the local file system&#41;&#46; The bytes encode the actual characters according to a particular <em>character encoding</em>&#44; which the user agent uses to decode the bytes into characters&#46;

<strong>Note&#58;</strong>

For XML documents&#44; the algorithm user agents are required to use to determine the character encoding is given by XML&#46; This section does not apply to XML documents&#46; [&#91;XML&#93;](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/commit-snapshots/877d6146487f15b15bc8dd0e3c625063a37b456a/#refsXML)

Usually&#44; the <a id="the&#45;input&#45;byte&#45;stream&#58;encoding&#45;sniffing&#45;algorithm"></a>[encoding sniffing algorithm](#encoding-sniffing-algorithm) defined below is used to determine the character encoding&#46;

Given a character encoding&#44; the bytes in the <a id="the&#45;input&#45;byte&#45;stream&#58;the&#45;input&#45;byte&#45;stream"></a>[input byte stream](#the-input-byte-stream) must be converted to characters for the tokenizer&#39;s <a id="the&#45;input&#45;byte&#45;stream&#58;input&#45;stream"></a>[input stream](#input-stream)&#44; by passing the <a id="the&#45;input&#45;byte&#45;stream&#58;the&#45;input&#45;byte&#45;stream&#45;2"></a>[input byte stream](#the-input-byte-stream) and character encoding to <a id="the&#45;input&#45;byte&#45;stream&#58;decode"></a>[decode](https://encoding.spec.whatwg.org/#decode)&#46;

<strong>Note&#58;</strong>

A leading Byte Order Mark &#40;BOM&#41; causes the character encoding argument to be ignored and will itself be skipped&#46;

<strong>Note&#58;</strong>

Bytes or sequences of bytes in the original byte stream that did not conform to the Encoding standard &#40;e&#46;g&#46; invalid UTF&#45;8 byte sequences in a UTF&#45;8 input byte stream&#41; are errors that conformance checkers are expected to report&#46; [&#91;ENCODING&#93;](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/commit-snapshots/877d6146487f15b15bc8dd0e3c625063a37b456a/#refsENCODING)

<strong>Warning&#58;</strong>

The decoder algorithms describe how to handle invalid input&#59; for security reasons&#44; it is imperative that those rules be followed precisely&#46; Differences in how invalid byte sequences are handled can result in&#44; amongst other problems&#44; script injection vulnerabilities &#40;&#34;XSS&#34;&#41;&#46;

When the HTML parser is decoding an input byte stream&#44; it uses a character encoding and a <a id="concept&#45;encoding&#45;confidence"></a><strong>confidence</strong>&#46; The confidence is either <em>tentative</em>&#44; <em>certain</em>&#44; or <em>irrelevant</em>&#46; The encoding used&#44; and whether the confidence in that encoding is <em>tentative</em> or <em>certain</em>&#44; is [used during the parsing](#meta-charset-during-parse) to determine whether to <a id="the&#45;input&#45;byte&#45;stream&#58;change&#45;the&#45;encoding"></a>[change the encoding](#change-the-encoding)&#46; If no encoding is necessary&#44; e&#46;g&#46; because the parser is operating on a Unicode stream and doesn&#39;t have to use a character encoding at all&#44; then the <a id="the&#45;input&#45;byte&#45;stream&#58;concept&#45;encoding&#45;confidence"></a>[confidence](#concept-encoding-confidence) is <em>irrelevant</em>&#46;

<strong>Note&#58;</strong>

Some algorithms feed the parser by directly adding characters to the <a id="the&#45;input&#45;byte&#45;stream&#58;input&#45;stream&#45;2"></a>[input stream](#input-stream) rather than adding bytes to the <a id="the&#45;input&#45;byte&#45;stream&#58;the&#45;input&#45;byte&#45;stream&#45;3"></a>[input byte stream](#the-input-byte-stream)&#46;

##### <a id="parsing&#45;with&#45;a&#45;known&#45;character&#45;encoding"></a>13&#46;2&#46;3&#46;1 Parsing with a known character encoding[](#parsing-with-a-known-character-encoding)

When the HTML parser is to operate on an input byte stream that has <a id="a&#45;known&#45;definite&#45;encoding"></a><strong>a known definite encoding</strong>&#44; then the character encoding is that encoding and the <a id="parsing&#45;with&#45;a&#45;known&#45;character&#45;encoding&#58;concept&#45;encoding&#45;confidence"></a>[confidence](#concept-encoding-confidence) is <em>certain</em>&#46;

##### <a id="determining&#45;the&#45;character&#45;encoding"></a>13&#46;2&#46;3&#46;2 Determining the character encoding[](#determining-the-character-encoding)

In some cases&#44; it might be impractical to unambiguously determine the encoding before parsing the document&#46; Because of this&#44; this specification provides for a two&#45;pass mechanism with an optional pre&#45;scan&#46; Implementations are allowed&#44; as described below&#44; to apply a simplified parsing algorithm to whatever bytes they have available before beginning to parse the document&#46; Then&#44; the real parser is started&#44; using a tentative encoding derived from this pre&#45;parse and other out&#45;of&#45;band metadata&#46; If&#44; while the document is being loaded&#44; the user agent discovers a character encoding declaration that conflicts with this information&#44; then the parser can get reinvoked to perform a parse of the document with the real encoding&#46;

<a id="documentEncoding"></a>User agents must use the following algorithm&#44; called the <a id="encoding&#45;sniffing&#45;algorithm"></a><strong>encoding sniffing algorithm</strong>&#44; to determine the character encoding to use when decoding a document in the first pass&#46; This algorithm takes as input any out&#45;of&#45;band metadata available to the user agent &#40;e&#46;g&#46; the <a id="determining&#45;the&#45;character&#45;encoding&#58;content&#45;type"></a>[Content&#45;Type metadata](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/commit-snapshots/877d6146487f15b15bc8dd0e3c625063a37b456a/#content-type) of the document&#41; and all the bytes available so far&#44; and returns a character encoding and a <a id="determining&#45;the&#45;character&#45;encoding&#58;concept&#45;encoding&#45;confidence"></a>[confidence](#concept-encoding-confidence) that is either <em>tentative</em> or <em>certain</em>&#46;

1.  If the result of <a id="determining&#45;the&#45;character&#45;encoding&#58;bom&#45;sniff"></a>[BOM sniffing](https://encoding.spec.whatwg.org/#bom-sniff) is an encoding&#44; return that encoding with <a id="determining&#45;the&#45;character&#45;encoding&#58;concept&#45;encoding&#45;confidence&#45;2"></a>[confidence](#concept-encoding-confidence) <em>certain</em>&#46;

    <strong>Note&#58;</strong>

    Although the <a id="determining&#45;the&#45;character&#45;encoding&#58;decode"></a>[decode](https://encoding.spec.whatwg.org/#decode) algorithm will itself change the encoding to use based on the presence of a byte order mark&#44; this algorithm sniffs the BOM as well in order to set the correct <a id="determining&#45;the&#45;character&#45;encoding&#58;document&#39;s&#45;character&#45;encoding"></a>[document&#39;s character encoding](https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-document-encoding) and <a id="determining&#45;the&#45;character&#45;encoding&#58;concept&#45;encoding&#45;confidence&#45;3"></a>[confidence](#concept-encoding-confidence)&#46;

2.  If the user has explicitly instructed the user agent to override the document&#39;s character encoding with a specific encoding&#44; optionally return that encoding with the <a id="determining&#45;the&#45;character&#45;encoding&#58;concept&#45;encoding&#45;confidence&#45;4"></a>[confidence](#concept-encoding-confidence) <em>certain</em>&#46;

    <strong>Note&#58;</strong>

    Typically&#44; user agents remember such user requests across sessions&#44; and in some cases apply them to documents in <a id="determining&#45;the&#45;character&#45;encoding&#58;the&#45;iframe&#45;element"></a><code>[iframe](html-language-elements-embedded--877d6146487f--48a1a13e5cfe.md#the-iframe-element)</code>s as well&#46;

3.  The user agent may wait for more bytes of the resource to be available&#44; either in this step or at any later step in this algorithm&#46; For instance&#44; a user agent might wait 500ms or 1024 bytes&#44; whichever came first&#46; In general preparsing the source to find the encoding improves performance&#44; as it reduces the need to throw away the data structures used when parsing upon finding the encoding information&#46; However&#44; if the user agent delays too long to obtain data to determine the encoding&#44; then the cost of the delay could outweigh any performance improvements from the preparse&#46;

    <strong>Note&#58;</strong>

    The authoring conformance requirements for character encoding declarations limit them to only appearing [in the first 1024 bytes](html-language-elements-attributes--877d6146487f--2ca83b5ac984.md#charset1024)&#46; User agents are therefore encouraged to use the prescan algorithm below &#40;as invoked by these steps&#41; on the first 1024 bytes&#44; but not to stall beyond that&#46;

4.  If the transport layer specifies a character encoding&#44; and it is supported&#44; return that encoding with the <a id="determining&#45;the&#45;character&#45;encoding&#58;concept&#45;encoding&#45;confidence&#45;5"></a>[confidence](#concept-encoding-confidence) <em>certain</em>&#46;

5.  Optionally&#44; <a id="determining&#45;the&#45;character&#45;encoding&#58;prescan&#45;a&#45;byte&#45;stream&#45;to&#45;determine&#45;its&#45;encoding"></a>[prescan the byte stream to determine its encoding](#prescan-a-byte-stream-to-determine-its-encoding)&#44; with the <em><a id="determining&#45;the&#45;character&#45;encoding&#58;prescan&#45;end&#45;condition"></a>[end condition](#prescan-end-condition)</em> being when the user agent decides that scanning further bytes would not be efficient&#46; User agents are encouraged to only prescan the first 1024 bytes&#46; User agents may decide that scanning <em>any</em> bytes is not efficient&#44; in which case these substeps are entirely skipped&#46;

    The aforementioned algorithm returns either a character encoding or failure&#46; If it returns a character encoding&#44; then return the same encoding&#44; with <a id="determining&#45;the&#45;character&#45;encoding&#58;concept&#45;encoding&#45;confidence&#45;6"></a>[confidence](#concept-encoding-confidence) <em>tentative</em>&#46;

6.  If the <a id="determining&#45;the&#45;character&#45;encoding&#58;html&#45;parser"></a>[HTML parser](#html-parser) for which this algorithm is being run is associated with a <a id="determining&#45;the&#45;character&#45;encoding&#58;document"></a><code>[Document](html-language-foundations--877d6146487f--b55e73c31978.md#document)</code> <var>d</var> whose <a id="determining&#45;the&#45;character&#45;encoding&#58;doc&#45;container&#45;document"></a>[container document](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/commit-snapshots/877d6146487f15b15bc8dd0e3c625063a37b456a/#doc-container-document) is non&#45;null&#58;

    1.  Let <var>parentDocument</var> be <var>d</var>&#39;s <a id="determining&#45;the&#45;character&#45;encoding&#58;doc&#45;container&#45;document&#45;2"></a>[container document](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/commit-snapshots/877d6146487f15b15bc8dd0e3c625063a37b456a/#doc-container-document)&#46;

    2.  If <var>parentDocument</var>&#39;s <a id="determining&#45;the&#45;character&#45;encoding&#58;concept&#45;document&#45;origin"></a>[origin](https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-document-origin) is <a id="determining&#45;the&#45;character&#45;encoding&#58;same&#45;origin"></a>[same origin](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/commit-snapshots/877d6146487f15b15bc8dd0e3c625063a37b456a/#same-origin) with <var>d</var>&#39;s <a id="determining&#45;the&#45;character&#45;encoding&#58;concept&#45;document&#45;origin&#45;2"></a>[origin](https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-document-origin) and <var>parentDocument</var>&#39;s <a id="determining&#45;the&#45;character&#45;encoding&#58;document&#39;s&#45;character&#45;encoding&#45;2"></a>[character encoding](https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-document-encoding) is not <a id="determining&#45;the&#45;character&#45;encoding&#58;utf&#45;16&#45;encoding"></a>[UTF&#45;16BE&#47;LE](https://encoding.spec.whatwg.org/#utf-16be-le)&#44; then return <var>parentDocument</var>&#39;s <a id="determining&#45;the&#45;character&#45;encoding&#58;document&#39;s&#45;character&#45;encoding&#45;3"></a>[character encoding](https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-document-encoding)&#44; with the <a id="determining&#45;the&#45;character&#45;encoding&#58;concept&#45;encoding&#45;confidence&#45;7"></a>[confidence](#concept-encoding-confidence) <em>tentative</em>&#46;

7.  Otherwise&#44; if the user agent has information on the likely encoding for this page&#44; e&#46;g&#46; based on the encoding of the page when it was last visited&#44; then return that encoding&#44; with the <a id="determining&#45;the&#45;character&#45;encoding&#58;concept&#45;encoding&#45;confidence&#45;8"></a>[confidence](#concept-encoding-confidence) <em>tentative</em>&#46;

8.  The user agent may attempt to autodetect the character encoding from applying frequency analysis or other algorithms to the data stream&#46; Such algorithms may use information about the resource other than the resource&#39;s contents&#44; including the address of the resource&#46; If autodetection succeeds in determining a character encoding&#44; and that encoding is a supported encoding&#44; then return that encoding&#44; with the <a id="determining&#45;the&#45;character&#45;encoding&#58;concept&#45;encoding&#45;confidence&#45;9"></a>[confidence](#concept-encoding-confidence) <em>tentative</em>&#46; [&#91;UNIVCHARDET&#93;](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/commit-snapshots/877d6146487f15b15bc8dd0e3c625063a37b456a/#refsUNIVCHARDET)

    <strong>Note&#58;</strong>

    User agents are generally discouraged from attempting to autodetect encodings for resources obtained over the network&#44; since doing so involves inherently non&#45;interoperable heuristics&#46; Attempting to detect encodings based on an HTML document&#39;s preamble is especially tricky since HTML markup typically uses only ASCII characters&#44; and HTML documents tend to begin with a lot of markup rather than with text content&#46;

    <strong>Note&#58;</strong>

    The UTF&#45;8 encoding has a highly detectable bit pattern&#46; Files from the local file system that contain bytes with values greater than 0x7F which match the UTF&#45;8 pattern are very likely to be UTF&#45;8&#44; while documents with byte sequences that do not match it are very likely not&#46; When a user agent can examine the whole file&#44; rather than just the preamble&#44; detecting for UTF&#45;8 specifically can be especially effective&#46; [&#91;PPUTF8&#93;](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/commit-snapshots/877d6146487f15b15bc8dd0e3c625063a37b456a/#refsPPUTF8) [&#91;UTF8DET&#93;](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/commit-snapshots/877d6146487f15b15bc8dd0e3c625063a37b456a/#refsUTF8DET)

9.  Otherwise&#44; return an <a id="determining&#45;the&#45;character&#45;encoding&#58;implementation&#45;defined"></a>[implementation&#45;defined](https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#implementation-defined) or user&#45;specified default character encoding&#44; with the <a id="determining&#45;the&#45;character&#45;encoding&#58;concept&#45;encoding&#45;confidence&#45;10"></a>[confidence](#concept-encoding-confidence) <em>tentative</em>&#46;

    In controlled environments or in environments where the encoding of documents can be prescribed &#40;for example&#44; for user agents intended for dedicated use in new networks&#41;&#44; the comprehensive <code>UTF&#45;8</code> encoding is suggested&#46;

    In other environments&#44; the default encoding is typically dependent on the user&#39;s locale &#40;an approximation of the languages&#44; and thus often encodings&#44; of the pages that the user is likely to frequent&#41;&#46; The following table gives suggested defaults based on the user&#39;s locale&#44; for compatibility with legacy content&#46; Locales are identified by BCP 47 language tags&#46; [&#91;BCP47&#93;](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/commit-snapshots/877d6146487f15b15bc8dd0e3c625063a37b456a/#refsBCP47) [&#91;ENCODING&#93;](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/commit-snapshots/877d6146487f15b15bc8dd0e3c625063a37b456a/#refsENCODING)
